clarity.justification: The method aligns with the hypothesis: the plan will "knock out top form-circuit components" and repeat this for the meaning circuit while measuring grammaticality and inference changes, with circuit overlap and layer distributions as secondary measurements. The prediction is directional and refutable: form ablation should "collapse grammaticality discrimination while preserving inference above chance," whereas meaning ablation "should do the reverse"; failure to obtain this selective double dissociation would count against the claim. However, "collapse," "top" components, "inferential correctness," and the "double-dissociation index" are not operationally defined, and no effect-size or statistical decision threshold is supplied, so an implementer must resolve material questions about component selection and what magnitude constitutes dissociation.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is using "path patching to rank heads" and fitting and ranking SAE features for two task families; this requires custom experimental logic but consists of established activation-intervention, ablation, and representation-learning operations supported by standard interpretability tooling rather than an undefined magic step. The named artifacts—"1k BLiMP-style syntactic minimal pairs," GPT-2-large, Llama-3-8B, and Llama-3-70B—exist as usable model or benchmark foundations, while the proposed controlled inference set must be constructed according to the stated plan. Resources are usefully quantified by two 1,000-item datasets and three named model scales, although the SAE configuration, number of selected components, inference-task composition, and replication/statistical plan remain unspecified. The refuting branch is runnable because every selected ablation is evaluated on both task families and compared with the explicit control "ablate random matched-size component set to gauge nonspecific damage," though stronger activation-matched or general-capability controls would better distinguish circuit specificity from generic disruption.
